newsitem.title: POLAND: ZLOTY RISES AS CURRENCY-BUYING TREND COOLS.
newsitem.headline: ZLOTY RISES AS CURRENCY-BUYING TREND COOLS.

text.p: The Polish zloty got a lift from mysterious currency-sales on Monday with the market divided if the zloty demand came from the central bank or market players.

Dealers confirmed only one $5 million central bank currency-selling intervenion in late trade, after the zloty had already gained almost half a point against its currency basket since opening amid an unexpected zloty-buying trend.

"There were some orders of currency-selling, perhaps from a client or banks rebuilding zloty positions after cutting them last week...or it may have been the central bank all along," said Mateusz Bieniek, dealer at Societe Generale in Warsaw.
The zloty closed at -2.84/-2.94 percent from the trading band centre, against Friday's close at -3.30/-3.37 percent.
It closed at 3.4650/80 to the dollar, against 3.4850/55 on Friday and at 1.9315/35 to the mark, against 1.9365/90.
Dealers confirmed only one central bank intervention on Friday, at 3.4685 zlotys to the dollar when the local unit was at -3.02 percent from parity.

Regardless of how much influence the central bank had on the zloty's rise on Monday, dealers expected the local unit to continue to rise in the near-future despite potential foreign investor withdrawal from Polish treasuries if the zloty firms.
"There should be more NBP operations gently showing that the bank wants to see the zloty a bit stronger within the 14-percent band," said Pawel Gajewski of Creditanstalt.
Dealers said that the zloty should now float between two and 3.5 percent below the parity rate, with any further gains likely setting off foreign investor sales of Polish paper.
Minimum prices of all Polish T-bills fell at Monday's primary auction on higher than expected demand of 1.08 billion zlotys against a 1.1 billion zloty offer.
The ministry sold bills worth 842 million zlotys, pushing up the benchmark 52-week T-bill yield up 0.09 to 22.09 percent.

On the money market one-day rates held relatively flat just under 24 percent as a large cash inflow on Tuesday created some short-term surplus funds and kept rates from climbing higher despite wide-spread expectations of an interest rate rise.
Overnight rates closed flat at 23.30/23.70 percent and tomorrow/next inched down slightly to 23.65/23.95.
